subject: en
source: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 syllabus 2027–2029, Cambridge International

weeks.topic: Reading for explicit meaning: locating and selecting information
objectives: Find and select relevant details from a text
Answer short comprehension questions precisely

weeks.topic: Reading for implicit meaning: inference and attitudes
objectives: Infer thoughts, feelings and attitudes from evidence
Support inferences with textual reference

weeks.topic: Explaining words and phrases in your own words
objectives: Explain the meaning of words and phrases in context
Avoid copying from the text

weeks.topic: Writers' effects: imagery and figurative language
objectives: Identify similes, metaphors and personification
Explain the effect of images on the reader

weeks.topic: Writers' effects: connotation and word choice
objectives: Explore connotations of individual words
Explain how word choice shapes meaning and mood

weeks.topic: Writing a language analysis response (200–250 words)
objectives: Select powerful words and phrases from a passage
Analyse meaning and effect in a focused response

weeks.topic: Descriptive writing: sensory detail and focus
objectives: Use the senses to build a vivid picture
Sustain focus on a scene rather than a plot

weeks.topic: Descriptive writing: structure, zooming in and shifting perspective
objectives: Organise description with deliberate structure
Use zoom, time shifts and contrast

weeks.topic: Narrative writing: plot, openings and endings
objectives: Plan a narrative with a clear arc
Write engaging openings and satisfying endings

weeks.topic: Narrative writing: characterisation and dialogue
objectives: Develop convincing characters through detail and action
Punctuate and use dialogue purposefully

weeks.topic: Sentence variety and punctuation for effect
objectives: Vary sentence length and structure for effect
Use semicolons, colons and dashes accurately

weeks.topic: Vocabulary range: precise and ambitious word choice
objectives: Choose precise vocabulary suited to purpose
Avoid repetition and clichés

weeks.topic: Non-fiction text types: articles, reviews and discursive essays
objectives: Identify features of non-fiction forms
Compare purpose and audience across texts

weeks.topic: Accuracy: spelling, punctuation and grammar
objectives: Correct common errors in spelling and grammar
Proofread work systematically

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: reading skills and descriptive and narrative writing
objectives: Consolidate comprehension and language analysis
Redraft a descriptive or narrative piece

weeks.topic: Summary writing: selecting relevant points
objectives: Identify points relevant to a summary focus
Organise points logically

weeks.topic: Summary writing: concise, fluent summaries in own words (120 words)
objectives: Write a summary within the word limit
Use own words and avoid unnecessary detail

weeks.topic: Attitudes and opinions in non-fiction texts
objectives: Identify a writer's attitudes and opinions
Explain how they are conveyed

weeks.topic: Directed writing: formal and informal letters
objectives: Adapt tone and register for letters
Develop ideas from source material in a letter

weeks.topic: Directed writing: speeches and rhetoric
objectives: Use rhetorical devices for a listening audience
Structure a speech for impact

weeks.topic: Directed writing: articles with headlines and structure
objectives: Write articles for a given publication and audience
Use headlines and paragraphing effectively

weeks.topic: Directed writing: reports with an objective tone
objectives: Organise information clearly in a report
Maintain an objective, formal tone

weeks.topic: Evaluating and developing ideas from texts
objectives: Evaluate the strength of ideas in a text
Develop ideas beyond the source with own reasoning

weeks.topic: Discursive writing: balancing viewpoints
objectives: Present different viewpoints fairly
Reach a measured conclusion

weeks.topic: Argumentative writing: building a case and counter-argument
objectives: Construct a logical argument with evidence
Anticipate and rebut counter-arguments

weeks.topic: Persuasive writing: rhetorical and emotive techniques
objectives: Use persuasive techniques purposefully
Adapt persuasion to a specific audience

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: reading paper and directed writing
objectives: Sit a timed reading paper
Write a timed directed writing task

weeks.topic: Extended response to reading: writing in role from a text
objectives: Use information from a text in a new form
Combine reading accuracy with writing quality

weeks.topic: Writing forms: journals and interviews
objectives: Write convincing journal entries
Structure interviews with questions and answers

weeks.topic: Speaking and Listening: the individual talk
objectives: Plan and deliver a talk using a cue card
Engage the listener with structure and delivery

weeks.topic: Speaking and Listening: the conversation
objectives: Respond to questions and develop ideas orally
Listen and respond appropriately

weeks.topic: Drafting and redrafting a descriptive piece
objectives: Draft a descriptive piece of 500–800 words
Redraft using feedback for improvement

weeks.topic: Narrative structure: time shifts, flashback and cyclical structure
objectives: Experiment with non-linear structure
Control pace and tension

weeks.topic: Reading unseen fiction from the 20th and 21st centuries
objectives: Read extracts of modern fiction closely
Respond to character, setting and mood

weeks.topic: Comparing how writers achieve effects in two texts
objectives: Compare techniques across two texts
Write a structured comparison question response

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: reading and writing
objectives: Sit reading and writing papers on Year 10 skills
Apply time management

weeks.topic: Year 10 review and preview of Year 11 exam papers
objectives: Correct exam errors
Preview Paper 1 and Paper 2 question formats
